sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy restricts access to system components and cardholder data by business need to know, supporting the PCI DSS access-control requirements.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: All access to the cardholder data environment and cardholder data.

sections.heading: 3. Need to Know and Least Privilege
sections.body:
Access to system components and cardholder data is restricted to what each role requires:
- Access is granted on documented need-to-know and least privilege, through an approval process.
- Privileges are assigned by role and default to deny-all unless explicitly granted.
- Access rights are reviewed periodically and removed promptly on termination or role change.

sections.heading: 4. Authentication
sections.body:
Users are uniquely identified and strongly authenticated:
- Every user has a unique ID, and shared or generic accounts are avoided.
- Strong authentication is enforced, and multi-factor authentication protects all access into the CDE, and all remote and administrative access.
- Credentials are managed securely and vendor-default accounts and passwords are changed or disabled.
- [FILL IN: state your MFA coverage and method.]

sections.heading: 7. Compliance & Enforcement
sections.body: Compliance with this policy is mandatory. Violations may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or contract, and may be reported to relevant authorities where required by law.

sections.heading: 8. Exceptions
sections.body: Any exception to this policy must be requested in writing, risk-assessed, and approved by [Approver / CISO] at [Company Name]. Approved exceptions are documented, time-bound and reviewed at expiry.

sections.heading: 9. Review
sections.body: This policy is reviewed at least annually, or after a significant change or security incident, and updated as required.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy protects account data through encryption and key management, supporting the PCI DSS requirements to protect stored account data and encrypt transmission over open networks.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: Account data at rest and in transit within and beyond the cardholder data environment.

sections.heading: 3. Protecting Stored Data
sections.body:
Account data is minimised and protected wherever it is stored:
- The primary account number (PAN) is rendered unreadable wherever it is stored, for example through strong cryptography.
- Sensitive authentication data (such as the full track, CVV or PIN) is not retained after authorisation.
- Storage of account data is kept to the minimum necessary, with a defined retention and disposal process.
- [FILL IN: state how PAN is rendered unreadable and your account-data retention.]

sections.heading: 4. Transmission and Key Management
sections.body:
Account data is protected in transit and the keys that protect it are controlled:
- PAN is encrypted with strong cryptography during transmission over open, public networks.
- Cryptographic keys are generated, distributed, stored, rotated and retired through a protected, documented process.
- Access to keys is restricted to the fewest custodians necessary and separated from the data they protect.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This incident response plan ensures the organisation can respond to a suspected or confirmed compromise of cardholder data, supporting the PCI DSS incident-response requirement.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: Security incidents affecting the cardholder data environment or cardholder data.

sections.heading: 3. Response Process
sections.body:
The plan covers the lifecycle of a suspected cardholder-data compromise:
- Defined roles and severity levels so the response is coordinated.
- Detection, containment, eradication and recovery steps.
- A post-incident review, and testing of the plan at least annually.

sections.heading: 4. Notification
sections.body:
The plan provides for timely notification of the parties a card-data compromise requires:
- The relevant payment brands and the acquiring bank.
- Regulators and affected individuals where required by law.
- [FILL IN: list your acquirer, payment-brand and regulator contacts.]

sections.heading: 5. Readiness and Triggers
sections.body: Designated personnel are available to respond on a 24/7 basis, and the plan is triggered by alerts from security monitoring such as intrusion-detection, change-detection and fraud-detection systems; it is reviewed and updated after each incident and at least annually.

sections.body: This plan is reviewed at least annually and after every activation or major change. Exercises (tabletop or full) are scheduled to validate the plan and results are recorded as improvement actions.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy establishes the information security programme that protects cardholder data, supporting the PCI DSS requirement for an overall information security policy.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: The cardholder data environment (CDE) and the people and systems that support it.

sections.heading: 3. Security Programme
sections.body:
The organisation maintains an overall information security policy and programme that protects account data:
- The policy covers security roles, risk management, acceptable use of technology, and the protection of account data.
- It is published, kept current, and reviewed at least once every 12 months and after significant change.
- The cardholder data environment (CDE) is scoped and documented so the programme is applied to everything in it.
- [FILL IN: reference your CDE scope and the cardholder data inventory.]

sections.heading: 4. Responsibilities and Awareness
sections.body:
Security responsibilities are formally assigned, and personnel understand their obligations:
- A named owner is accountable for the PCI programme, with day-to-day responsibilities assigned to defined roles.
- Personnel receive security awareness training and acknowledge the acceptable-use and security policies.
- The programme is supported by the subordinate PCI policies (access, network, encryption, vulnerability, logging and incident response).

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy ensures access to system components and cardholder data is logged and monitored, supporting the PCI DSS logging and monitoring requirements.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: System components in the cardholder data environment and the access to them.

sections.heading: 3. Logging
sections.body:
Activity in the cardholder data environment is recorded so it can be reconstructed:
- Audit logs capture access to cardholder data, administrative actions, and key security events, with enough detail to attribute each event.
- Clocks are synchronised to a consistent time source, and logs are protected from alteration and unauthorised access.
- Logs are retained for at least 12 months, with at least the most recent three months immediately available for analysis.
- [FILL IN: confirm your retention period and log sources.]

sections.heading: 4. Monitoring and Testing
sections.body:
Logs and the environment are actively watched:
- Logs are reviewed, using automated mechanisms where required, and security events are alerted on and triaged.
- Critical files are monitored for unauthorised change, and the network is monitored and tested for unexpected activity.
- A failure of a critical security control is detected, alerted on and responded to promptly.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy ensures network security controls protect and segment the cardholder data environment, supporting the PCI DSS network-security requirements.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: The network components that protect or connect to the cardholder data environment.

sections.heading: 3. Network Controls
sections.body:
Network security controls protect the cardholder data environment:
- Firewalls or equivalent controls restrict inbound and outbound traffic to and from the CDE to only what is necessary, denying all else.
- Rulesets are documented with a business justification and reviewed at least every six months.
- Connections to untrusted networks and any wireless access into the CDE are controlled and secured.
- [FILL IN: reference your network diagram and rule-review process.]

sections.heading: 4. Segmentation
sections.body:
Segmentation is used to keep scope and risk down:
- The CDE is segmented from other networks so that out-of-scope systems cannot reach it.
- Where segmentation is relied on to reduce scope, it is validated periodically (and by penetration testing where required).

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy protects systems from malicious software and manages vulnerabilities, supporting the PCI DSS vulnerability-management requirements.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: System components in and connected to the cardholder data environment.

sections.heading: 3. Malware and Patching
sections.body:
System components are protected from malware and known vulnerabilities:
- Anti-malware protection is deployed on susceptible systems, kept current, and actively running.
- Security patches are applied promptly, with critical and high-risk patches prioritised within defined timeframes.
- [FILL IN: name your anti-malware and patching tools and cadence.]

sections.heading: 4. Scanning and Secure Development
sections.body:
Vulnerabilities are found and fixed before they can be exploited:
- Internal vulnerability scans, and external scans by an Approved Scanning Vendor (ASV), are performed at least quarterly and after significant change.
- Findings are risk-ranked and remediated, and external scans are repeated until a passing result is achieved.
- Bespoke and custom software is developed and maintained securely, addressing common vulnerabilities.
